raw_response:
I have been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou for 50 years, and I grow cotton every year. I went to middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bag labels and do the calculations myself, but honestly I mostly go by what I have seen work on my own field and my neighbors' fields. Last year my 5 mu of cotton gave me a bit over 500 jin per mu — around 530 jin — and this year I will do about the same thing, maybe a small adjustment here and there.

For the seed, I will buy improved cotton seed. My neighbor across the road used **国抗棉99-1** last year and his bolls were big and white, so I will use that too. I do not use the old local seed anymore — the yield is too low.

For the ground, I will do **rotary tillage** twice before sowing. The first time is to break up the wheat stubble from last autumn, and the second time is to level the soil fine so the plastic film lays flat. I do it myself with the small rotary tiller I bought a few years back.

For fertilizer, here is my plan. I will put **80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu** as the base fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind from the dealer, which costs about 180 yuan per bag. That gives me about **7.5 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium** from the base dressing. Then at the flowering stage I will topdress with **20 jin of urea per mu** (46% nitrogen), which adds another **4.5 kg of nitrogen**. All together that is about **12 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu**. I know that is not a small amount, but cotton is a heavy feeder, and if I cut back and the yield drops, I lose much more money than I save on fertilizer. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than lose 100 jin of cotton.

I will irrigate **3 times** this year. First is the bottom water before sowing in late April to make sure the soil is moist for germination. Second is at early flowering in July when the plants are thirsty. Third is at peak boll stage in August so the bolls do not dry out. I have a well, so the water costs me mostly labor and a little electricity for the pump.

For pesticides, cotton here has bollworm, aphids, and red spider mites every year. I cannot skip spraying. I will spray **12 times** in total this year: about **10 times for insects**, once for weeds before sowing with herbicide, and maybe once for disease prevention if the weather turns humid. I buy the medicine from the agricultural supply shop in town. Each spray costs about 15–20 yuan per mu for the chemical plus my own labor. On a 5 mu farm, I do the spraying myself with a backpack sprayer — it takes me half a day each time.

My household has 4 people. My wife and I do most of the work, and my son helps during the busy harvest time. Since the farm is only 5 mu, we do not hire labor except maybe for one day at harvest if the weather threatens rain. I have to watch my total spending: the seed, fertilizer, plastic film, pesticides, and electricity for irrigation will cost me about 1,200–1,400 yuan per mu. If I get 500–550 jin of seed cotton per mu and the price is around 4 yuan per jin, I can make about 2,000 yuan per mu. That is not rich, but it pays for my grandson's school fees and our daily costs.

So my plan for this year: same variety, rotary tillage, compound fertilizer plus urea, 3 irrigations, 12 pesticide applications. I expect about **275 kg of seed cotton per mu** this year if the weather cooperates.
